text: Behavior contrary to the Benildean Expressions of the Lasallian Core Values.
Intentional disruption of or causing a disturbance to academic functions or College activities/events on/offcampus.
Disruption of or causing a disturbance to academic functions or College activities/events on/off campus.
Intentionally attending a class in which a student is not officially enrolled without the teacher’s permission.
Intentionally joining a school function without the permission of organizers or concerned authorities.
Littering, throwing, and/or dumping of waste matters consistent with the provisions stated in RA 9003, s 2021 or the “Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000.”
Entering the campus with an expired temporary pass issued by the college.
Unauthorized/irresponsible use of College facilities or property.

Eating or drinking in the College theaters, cinema, laboratories (except for SHRIM labs), and other identified non-eating or drinking areas; (for classrooms/auditorium, eating of meals may be allowed subject to the approval of the faculty in-charge or college authorities).

Misbehavior (e.g. jeering, interrupting of performances, making of obscene or vulgar gestures, etc.) during intercollegiate activities such as the National Collegiate Athletic Association games and similar events, provided such misbehavior does not constitute acts defined under major offenses.

Failure to surrender lost and found items to the Center for Restorative Discipline (CRD) or, in cases where the CRD is closed or otherwise inaccessible, to the Security Office, on the same day the lost and found item is found.

Violation of approved policies, guidelines, rules, and regulations of the different schools, offices/centers/ departments, laboratories, and/or the Center for Learning Resources (CLR) provided such violation does not constitute acts defined under major offenses. It is the organization/office/ unit head’s responsibility to enforce their respective rules, and as such, they are authorized to impose the necessary penalty on erring students, provided such penalty is incorporated or integrated in the approved policies disseminated to students concerned.

Minor Offenses with prior warnings listed below are misdemeanors that are not immediately counted as a minor offense against a student: 7.8.1.13.1 Wearing of inappropriate attire inside the campus. (See Appendix D General and Program Dress Code Policy). Please note that repeated violation of the general dress codes can lead to minor or major offenses as stated below: 1st infraction (with written warning) 2nd infraction (with written warning) 3rd infraction (with written warning) 4th infraction - 1st dress code-related minor offense + formation 5th infraction (with written warning) 6th infraction (with written warning) 7th infraction - 2nd dress code-related minor offense 8th infraction - 1st major offense 7.8.1.13.2 Violation of Program Dress Code Policy and standards of good grooming. (See Appendix D General and Program Dress Code Policy). Please note that repeated violation of the program dress codes and standards of good grooming can lead to minor or major offenses as stated below: 1st infraction (with written warning) 2nd infraction (with written warning) 3rd infraction (with written warning) 4th infraction - 1st dress code-related minor offense + formation 5th infraction (with written warning) 6th infraction (with written warning) 7th infraction - 2nd dress code-related minor offense 8th infraction - 1st major offense 7.8.1.13.3 Entering the campus without a Benilde ID. Please note that repeated Benilde ID violation can lead to minor or major offenses as stated below: 1st infraction (with written warning) 2nd infraction (with written warning) 3rd infraction (with written warning) 4th infraction - 1st Benilde ID-related minor offense + formation 5th infraction (with written warning) 6th infraction (with written warning) 7th infraction - 2nd Benilde ID-related minor offense 8th infraction - 1st major offense 7.8.1.13.4 Failure to wear Benilde ID at all times while inside College premises. Please note that repeated non-wearing of Benilde ID violation can lead to minor or major offenses as stated below: 1st infraction (with written warning) 2nd infraction (with written warning) 3rd infraction (with written warning) 4th infraction - 1st ID infraction + formation 5th infraction (with written warning) 6th infraction (with written warning) 7th infraction - 2nd ID infraction minor offense 8th infraction - 1st major offense 7.8.1.13.5 Violations in the Benilde dormitory by student residents can lead to minor or major offenses as stated below: 1st infraction (with written warning) 2nd infraction (with written warning) 3rd infraction (with written warning) 4th infraction - 1st dorm-related minor offense + formation 5th infraction (with written warning) 6th infraction (with written warning) 7th infraction - 2nd dorm-related minor offense 8th infraction - 1st major offense 7.8.1.13.6 Violations in the Benilde parking rules and regulations can lead to minor or major offenses as stated below: 1st infraction (with written warning) 2nd infraction (with written warning) 3rd infraction (with written warning) 4th infraction - 1st parking rules and regulations-related minor offense + formation 5th infraction (with written warning) 6th infraction (with written warning) 7th infraction - 2nd parking rules and regulations-related minor offense 8th infraction - 1st major offense

Reservation Clause. Any other act similar to the foregoing may be determined by the College as constituting a minor offense, provided that it is not applied retroactively. This includes other acts as may be determined by the CRD Director, provided the application is prospective and properly disseminated to students through official memoranda and/or student publications. A major offense, which merits any of the sanctions defined in Section 7.9.1, includes the following:

category: Offenses against College Security and Order
text: Initiating or participating in activities that threaten College security or public order.

category: Offenses against College Security and Order
text: Unauthorized possession of deadly weapons or objects that can be used to cause injury within the College premises or during College-sanctioned activities or functions on/off campus. (See Appendix F Implementing Rules and Regulations on Handling Deadly Weapons)

category: Offenses against College Security and Order
text: Lending, borrowing, or using someone else’s ID, Student Enrollment Record, student ID number, Infonet account, Benilde email, official receipt, or other official documents.

category: Offenses against College Security and Order
text: Double tapping of Benilde ID and/or providing any form of assistance for entry to the campus.

category: Offenses against College Security and Order
text: Malicious dissemination of false information of the willful making of any threat concerning bombs, explosives, or any similar device or means of destruction.

Direct assault upon the person of any member of the faculty, administration, non-teaching personnel, or any College personnel, or any student or person vested with authority while such person is in the performance of official duties or on occasion of such performance.

Indirect assault, or using force or intimidation against any person coming to the aid of the authorities on occasion of the commission of the offense defined in the immediately preceding section Offenses against Public Interest and the Good Reputation of the College.
Dishonesty and/or any fraudulent act.

Forging, falsifying, or tampering with academic or official records or documents including school ID; securing or using forged, falsified or tampered school records, forms, and/or official documents; or practicing or attempting to practice any deception or fraud in connection with one’s admission to, registration in, or graduation from the College or any College activity or function. The student is accountable for the authenticity of all documents submitted, regardless of whether he/she is directly involved in the act defined herein.
Perjury, defined as testifying falsely in any administrative proceeding or knowingly making untruthful statements in documents under oath when such oath is required.

Any act, omission, condition, status, or circumstance tending to cause or causing disrepute, discredit, or dishonor to the College or persons in authority, and/or contempt for the name of the College or any member of the community.
Making false representation and/or announcement that tends to put in disrepute or cause damage to the College or persons in authority.
Making false representation as an authorized, recognized, and/ or accredited Benilde student organization/group.
Any form of student- or student organization/group- related misconduct, whether committed within or outside College premises, which directly or indirectly affect the good name of the College
Unauthorized collection or solicitation of funds or exaction of money, checks or other negotiable instruments, and/or any material or object in connection with matters pertaining to the College.
Unauthorized selling of merchandise or services inside campus premises for any purpose.
Unauthorized recruitment and participation in activities of unrecognized and/or non-accredited group/association within campus premises.
Unauthorized operation of any group/association identifying as a Benilde recognized/accredited student group.
Embezzlement of funds of any legitimate College organization/ group or class.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Commission of any act constituting an “intellectual property offense” under the College’s Intellectual Property (IP) Rights Policy and Implementing Rules and Regulations 2018-2021 (IPR Policy and IRR available at https://ip.benilde.edu.ph/policy). 7.8.2.20.1 Unauthorized reproduction, including photocopying or any manner of copying, exhibit, use, or distribution, of any printed matter in whole or in part, including software and multimedia presentations, without permission of the author/creator/owner of the intellectual property, subject to the Use Rights under the IP Rights Policy, fair use principles for copyrighted works, and other exceptions provided in the Code. 7.8.2.20.2 Use, distribution, transfer, rental, sale, or production of counterfeit, unlicensed, or pirated intellectual property contained in an optical media as defined in R.A. No. 9239. 7.8.2.20.3 Deliberate failure to comply with the disclosure and manifestation requirements of the IPR Policy and IRR. 7.8.2.20.4 Failure to disclose, identify, or cite co-authors, co-creators or co-inventors in a research, creative work, or invention despite knowledge of the identities and contributions of these persons. 7.8.2.20.5 Unauthorized use, distribution, transfer, rental, sale or production of Benilde IP and merchandise bearing Benilde marks. 7.8.2.20.6 Non-compliance to the usage policy and institutional styleguide for Benilde marks. 7.8.2.20.7 Plagiarism and acts constituting academic dishonesty, including violations related to the misuse of AI tools, such as but not limited to: failing to disclose AI use when required, submitting AI-generated content as one’s own, falsifying AI declarations, or using AI to circumvent learning. 7.8.2.20.8 Violation of the right of authors, inventors, and creators to the integrity of their work in the exercise of use rights and fair use. 7.8.2.20.9 Failure of any person to cite or acknowledge the College in inventions and works: (a) developed or produced with the substantial use of College resources; (b) receiving grants or incentives from or funded through the College; or (c) when the College assigned, released, or waived its intellectual property rights in favor of such person 7.8.2.20.10 Knowingly aiding or abetting anyone; or failure to report anyone who commits intellectual property offenses. 7.8.2.20.11 Violation of the provision on confidentiality under Rule 12 of the IPR Policy IRR. 7.8.2.20.12 All other acts analogous to the foregoing.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Commission of any act violating R.A. No. 10173 or the Data Privacy Act of 2012 and the DLS-CSB Data Privacy policy: 7.8.2.21.1 Accessing/processing/divulging personal information of others without consent. 7.8.2.21.2 Selling personal information that they are in possession of or they have access to. 7.8.2.21.3 Using or disclosing personal information collected through College activities/events or service for profiling. 7.8.2.21.4 Collecting, marinating, using, or sharing of personal information beyond what is needed for education or school purposes or as authorized or with consent of the student. 7.8.2.21.5 Unsecured storage, retention beyond declared use, and unlawful destruction and/or alteration of personal information. 7.8.2.21.6 Negligence resulting in unauthorized disclosure of personal information. (See Appendix G Benilde Data Privacy Policy)

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Commission of any act violating DLS-CSB Social Media Policy Posting contents on social media which contain inaccurate and unconfirmed information; are not in line with Benildean values and ethics and relevant policies; promote or instruct harassment or bullying, or otherwise intimidate (ex. trolling); incite violence or hatred; contain abusive parts/materials relating to an individual’s age, disability, gender, civil/social status, race, religion/belief, sex/sexual orientation, or political belief; contain inappropriate images/photos/videos/audio recordings; disrespect others or are discourteous/rude; criticizeor argue with colleagues, students, parents, clients, partners, stakeholders, or competitors with ill will or in a non-constructive manner that may result in serious arguments; and/or breach confidentiality or copyright. (See Appendix H DLS-CSB Social Media Policy).

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Unauthorized possession or distribution or being under the influence of prohibited drugs or chemicals included in the list of prohibited drugs and chemicals by the National Bureau of Investigation and/or R.A. No. 9165 or the Dangerous Drugs Act of 2002, as amended; or the unauthorized possession of drug paraphernalia, distribution/selling, or possession of any regulated drug without proper prescription inside the College’s premises or outside during an off-campus academic function or College activity/event.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Smoking, vaping, or the use of electronic cigarettes, including the act of holding or displaying such devices, is strictly prohibited within all campus premises, at Benilde entrances and their immediate vicinity, inside Benilde-owned or operated vehicles, and during any school-sanctioned activity whether held on or off campus. (See Section 2.3.5.8)

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Unauthorized possession and/or drinking of alcoholic beverages within the College premises or during off-campus activities/events sponsored by the College.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Being in an intoxicated state within College premises or found to be positive for alcohol intake when tested by a health professional and/or designated associate.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Breach of the Benilde Infonet Policy or violation of its rules and regulations: 7.8.2.27.1 Accessing a College computer, computer network, or any IT services provided by the College (e.g. intranet portal, VPN service, etc.) without authority or beyond authorized access. 7.8.2.27.2 Introducing false information or preventing authorized use of information that is stored in any College storage systems/databases; transmitted to and/or from the College computer and/or telecommunications networks; and/or processed by any College information systems. 7.8.2.27.3 Preventing normal operations of computers, computer networks, or any IT services of the College. 7.8.2.27.4 Sending offensive content, threats, etc. using the Benilde Infonet or any computer network or services (e.g. blogs, social networking services, distribution/mailing lists, electronic groups/ forums, or electronic bulletin board services, etc.) outside the Benilde Infonet. 7.8.2.27.5 Altering, damaging, destroying, or disclosing information to others. 7.8.2.27.6 Infonet account disclosure or the disclosing of usernames, passwords, personal identification numbers, or any similar information that will allow access to Benilde Infonet or any institution/ organization to which the College has an authorized connection with full knowledge that the disclosure is without written approval from a person in authority 7.8.2.27.7 Violating the rules and regulations stated in the Benilde Infonet Manual. Note: For more information regarding Infonet policies and procedures, please refer to the Benilde Infonet Manual. (See Appendix I Information Network (Infonet) Policies, Conditions for Use, and Code of Practice for Appropriate Use)

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Gambling or participation in any form of gambling— including online gambling—whether on campus, off campus, or during any College-sanctioned activity or function, is strictly prohibited.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Membership in a fraternity/sorority, participating in any manner of recruitment of students into fraternities/sororities, or encouraging others to join any such organization that tends to violate their Non-Fraternity Contract. This includes membership in any organization not recognized by the College and that which subscribes to violent acts. (See Appendices J Republic Act No. 11053 - Anti-Hazing Act of 2018 and K CHED Memorandum Order 04 Series of 1995 Preventive Measures against Violence and Sanctions on Fraternities and other Student Organizations)

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Hazing, as defined by R.A. No. 11053 or any act of initiation that causes injury to an individual for the reason of admission, continuance, or retention of membership in any organization, association,society, or group. This is regardless of whether or not such acts result in the demise, physical disability, insanity, or psychological suffering of the individual. In reference to this section, all individuals present in the hazing who directly or indirectly participated in the hazing process are liable. All officers of the associations, societies, or groups, whether or not they were present during the initiation, are likewise liable. (See Section 7.10.1.2.1)

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Irreverent conduct that tends to prevent or disturb religious activities such as the Angelus, Masses, prayers, and other similar practices or other manifestations of any religion, including desecration of religious objects or places of worship.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Proselytizing, defined as attempting to convert others to one’s faith by attacking or denigrating the practices and beliefs of another or by offering special inducements.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Disrespect to national symbols (e.g. not standing at attention when the national anthem is being played) or any other similar infraction related to Republic Act No. 8491 or the Flag and Heraldic Code of the Philippines.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Violation of specific terms/conditions while on formation or probation.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Failure to comply with the summons (via email or summon form) in connection with discipline-related cases.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Defiance or willful non-compliance with the requirements set by the College in connection with one’s sanction or case.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Accumulation of three (3) minor offenses within the period of stay in the College. This does not apply to Minor Offenses with prior warnings (e.g. dress code violation), as stipulated in Section 7.8.1.13.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Accumulation of eight (8) ID infractions within the period of stay in the College, as stipulated in Section 7.8.1.13.3.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Accumulation of eight (8) general dress code infractions within the period of stay in the College, as stipulated in Section 7.8.1.13.1.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Accumulation of eight (8) program dress code and standards of good grooming infractions within the period of stay in the College, as stipulated in Section 7.8.1.13.2.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Accumulation of eight (8) dorm related infractions as stipulated in Section 7.8.1.13.5.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Accumulation of eight (8) non-wearing of ID as stipulated in Section 7.8.1.13.4.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Accumulation of eight (8) parking rules and regulations infractions as stipulated in Section 7.8.1.13.6.

category: Offenses against School Norms, Standards, and Policies
text: Willful failure to comply with required drug testing procedures. (See Appendices L Benilde Implementing Guidelines on Mandatory Drug Testing and The Implementing Guidelines for the Conduct of Drug Testing of Students in all Higher Education Institutions (HEIs)

category: Offenses against Good Morals and Norms of Decency
text: Acts of cheating such as, but not limited to, the following: A. Unauthorized possession of notes or any material relevant to an examination, whether or not the student actually uses them during the examination. B. Looking at examination papers of others and/or allowing another to glance/look at one’s own paper/notes during examination. C. Copying or allowing another to copy from one’s examination papers, assigned reports, case analyses, reaction papers, theses, and other similar materials. D. Communicating with another during examinations without permission from the teacher or proctor. E. Furnishing another person with answers to examination questions. F. Leaking examination questions to other students. G. Unauthorized use of cellular phones, communication gadgets, or any electronic device during examinations and other academic activity. H. Plagiarism, defined as intentionally or knowingly representing as one’s own work another person’s ideas, data, or language in any academic endeavor or exercise without proper acknowledgement. I. Misuse of AI tools, such as, but not limited to, failing to disclose AI use when required, submitting AI-generated content as one’s own, falsifying AI declarations, or using AI to circumvent learning. J. Taking an examination for another student, in which case both parties shall be liable. K. Infringement of the Intellectual Property Policy and its IRR. (See Section 7.8.2.20) L. Other acts of academic dishonesty committed online.

category: Offenses against Good Morals and Norms of Decency
text: A final and executory conviction before any court for a criminal offense involving moral turpitude against persons or property other than through reckless imprudence.

category: Offenses against Good Morals and Norms of Decency
text: Acts of indecency, lewdness, or immorality in any medium.

category: Offenses against Good Morals and Norms of Decency
text: Unless with a permit from the CRD and/or approval from a faculty concerned and as part of a course requirement: bringing in, viewing, displaying, sending, creating, copying, willful participation and/or distributing of pornographic or foul and malicious messages in whatever form or means including accessing pornographic and other prohibited Internet sites.

category: Offenses against Good Morals and Norms of Decency
text: Inappropriate display of intimacy within the College premises that offend or tend to offend the sensibilities of the community, and which may be deemed or perceived as vulgar, repulsive, or immoral.

category: Offenses against Good Morals and Norms of Decency
text: Acts of lewdness, displays of indecency, and any commission of immorality in any form or medium.

Commission of any act violating the Safe Spaces Act and its IRR and/or gender-based streets and public spaces sexual harassment, which include among others: (See Appendices N Safe Spaces Act and O Benilde Implementing Guidelines on Safe Spaces Act) a. Catcalling; wolf-whistling; unwanted invitations;and/or misogynistic, transphobic, homophobic, and/or sexist slurs; b. Persistent uninvited comments or gestures on a person’s appearance; c. Relentless requests for personal details; d. Statement of sexual comments and suggestions; e. Public masturbation or flashing of private parts, groping, making offensive body gestures at someone, and other similar lewd sexual actions; f. Any advance, whether verbal or physical, that is unwanted and has threatened one’s sense of personal space and physical safety. This may include cursing, leering and intrusive gazing, and taunting; g. Persistent telling of sexual jokes and/or use of sexual names; and h. Stalking.
Any act amounting to a crime or wrongdoing,or with infliction of any injury or harm upon the person, honor, and integrity of another on/off campus or in any social media platform.
Engaging or involving oneself in physical fights and/or acts of violence.

Vilifying any person with disability which could result in loss of self-esteem of the latter, including making an utterance of slanderous and abusive statements against a person with disability; and/or doing an activity in public which incites hatred towards, serious contempt for, or severe ridicule of persons with disability

Bullying, which refers to any severe or repeated use by one or more students of a written, verbal, signed, or electronic expression; a physical or psychological act or gesture; or any combination thereof, directed at another student, that has the effect of actually causing or placing the latter in reasonable fear of physical or emotional harm or damage to his property; creating a hostile environment in school for the other student; infringing on the rights of another student in school; and/or materially and substantially disrupting the education process or the orderly operation of a school; such as, but not limited to, the following (See Appendix P Anti-Bullying Policy): A. Any unwanted physical contact between the bully and the victim like punching, pushing, shoving, kicking, slapping, tickling, headlocks, inflicting school pranks, teasing, fighting, or using available objects as weapons. B. Any act that causes damage to a victim’s psyche and/or emotional wellbeing. C. Any verbal statement or accusation that causes the victim undue emotional distress like directing foul language or profanity at the target, name-calling, tormenting, and commenting negatively on a victim’s looks, clothes, or body. D. Cyber-bullying or any bullying done through the use of technology or any electronic means,including any conduct resulting in harassment, intimidation, or humiliation, through the use of various forms of technology, such as, but not limited to posts, texts, emails, instant messages, or chats on the Internet, social media, apps, online gaming platforms, and other platforms or formats. E. Discrimination regarding a person’s sexual orientation, gender identity, ethnicity, religion, lifestyle, disability, or any category that pertains to a person’s expression. This is usually, but not limited to, in the form of foul commentary, harassment, and/or physical confrontation motivated by a negative perspective on a certain group of people.

Vandalism or deliberate damage/destruction of College property or that belonging to any member of the community or to a visitor while on campus, or tampering with official announcements on bulletin boards. The student concerned shall pay for the damage incurred without prejudice to any other penalty or sanction imposed by the College.
Stealing, whether attempted or consummated, or knowingly possessing/receiving stolen goods or property. The student concerned shall pay for the damages, if there are any.

Unjust enrichment, which exists when a person unjustly retains a benefit to the loss of another, or when a person retains money or property of another against the fundamental principles of justice, equity, and good conscience, whether offline or online.

Harassment, intimidation, showing menace or provocation of any kind, whether or not such act results in verbal or physical confrontation between students and/or groups of students on/ off campus or in any online platform.

Gross acts of disrespect in words, gestures, signs, or deeds that put or tend to put any member of the faculty, administration, non-teaching associate, or other service provider, another student, or a visitor in ridicule or contempt.
Willful disregard of established policies, rules, and regulations.

Any other act or misconduct similar to all of the foregoing that may be deemed offensive and inappropriate by the College or any such acts as may be determined to be on the level of major offenses by the Discipline Board, provided the application is prospective and information on the same is disseminated to students through official memoranda and/or official student publication.
